description: Classification of the numbered pitfalls in the development repository's tickets/CONVENTIONS.md into failure classes for the appendix table. Every pitfall number in the development record must appear in exactly one class. Examples paraphrase the cited pitfall. Each class names the pitfall its example paraphrases; numbers in an example are transcribed from that pitfall.

classes.label: The number measured something else
classes.example: Timing only the kernel, when host-side reduction cost 3.5$\times$ as much

classes.label: An accuracy claim that does not generalize
classes.example: Grading against an unconverged reference that was off by +0.107 on the true top-50

classes.label: Numerical reasoning
classes.example: Two implementations agreeing because they share the same typo

classes.label: The code that ran was not the code under test
classes.example: A stale binary for an older GPU, silently JIT-compiled on the new one

classes.label: A silent failure that looks like a result
classes.example: A stop rule that no script evaluated, so a stage ran 129$\times$ its specified size

classes.label: Provenance and multi-agent hygiene
classes.example: A claimed ticket's file left on its own branch, so the ledger on main showed it unclaimed
